subject: KV-cache & session-trace export: scope, delivery options, and signed manifest
messages:
From: Sienna Park <sienna@medicosys.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@medicosys.com
Date: Wed, 7 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: March session traces + KV-cache linkage and signed manifest

Marcus —

Thanks for taking this on. For our SOC 2 readiness audit (period: 2025-03-01 -> 2025-03-31) we need a reproducible export that allows an external auditor to validate: which client-side request maps to which model variant, any admin actions that impacted routing/permissions, and the KV-cache session identifiers so we can trace invocation lineage.

Specifically we need:
- Per-request event with timestamp, request-id, model-variant id, routing decision, and user/session id (hashed is OK if reversible by us with a provided salt).
- Mapping of session_id -> KV-cache key snapshots (or pointers to snapshots) so auditors can verify cache hits/misses that affected outputs.
- Admin activity records for relevant user and role changes during March (create/delete/role-change) with actor, timestamp, and object-id.

We also need evidence of immutability/non-repudiation: a signed manifest that lists exported files and checksums plus an HMAC or signature from Redwood. Delivery: secure S3 presigned URL is preferred, but we can accept PGP-encrypted SFTP if that’s easier.

Please advise export formats, redaction options, and estimated delivery SLA. Also include a sampling plan if you recommend not exporting the full request body.

Thanks,
Sienna Park
Compliance Manager, MedicoSys

--
Sienna Park
MedicoSys Compliance
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sienna Park <sienna@medicosys.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 May 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: March session traces + KV-cache linkage and signed manifest

Sienna —

Appreciate the clear ask. We can produce the exports you describe. High level proposal below; I’ve attached a compact schema (kv_trace_schema.csv) and a short sample (sessionized_sample.jsonl) to illustrate fields.

1) Export formats (we propose two parallel artifacts):
   a) Compact event ledger (CSV): one row per event (request, routing decision, admin action). Fields: timestamp, event_type, request_id, session_id, user_hash, model_variant, route_reason, admin_actor, admin_action, object_id, checksum_ptr. Suitable for auditors who want tabular traces.
   b) Sessionized JSONL: session-per-line containing ordered requests, pointers to KV-cache snapshots (s3 paths) and derived model outputs. Better for reconstructing timelines.

2) KV-cache linkage: we will include pointer fields that reference signed KV snapshot objects (immutable blobs) stored in an evidence bucket. Each snapshot filename includes a deterministic session hash and sequence number (e.g., kvsess_<sessionhash>_0001.snap).

3) Admin activity: we will extract admin audit records scoped to identities with admin or routing privileges. Records include actor, role, action, affected_object_id, timestamp, and change_delta (when available).

4) Immutability & signed manifest: we will generate a manifest.json listing every exported file, size, and SHA256 checksum. Redwood will sign this manifest and produce an attached PDF (signed_manifest_v1.pdf). Additionally we can HMAC the manifest using a per-export key and provide the HMAC key wrap (PGP to your compliance mailbox) if required.

5) Redaction/sampling options: full payload export is often >TBs. We recommend:
   - Option A: full headers + metadata + pointers to payloads (payloads sampled at 10% and flagged)
   - Option B: full metadata + reversible user hashing (salt provided under NDA) + session-level sampled payloads (you can request a replay window)

6) Delivery and encryption: preferred - S3 presigned URLs (7-day validity) with objects encrypted using SSE-KMS (our key). If you need the KMS-wrapped key for verifier access we can PGP-encrypt the wrapping key to your compliance mailbox. Alternative - SFTP with PGP-encrypted tar.gz.

7) Timeline & SLA: initial manifest + sample (first 48 hours). Full scoped export for March data: 5 business days from signed evidence handoff agreement.

Questions for you before we start:
- Do you need request bodies (full prompt/response) or are metadata + payload pointers sufficient?
- For user identity hashing, will MedicoSys retain the salt on file or do you want Redwood to hold it (we prefer you retain it under NDA).
- Confirm delivery preference (S3 vs SFTP) and the contact for PGP public key.

I’ll defer to Hannah on sampling/retention specifics and Laura on packaging and manifest signature keys.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: kv_trace_schema.csv, sessionized_sample.jsonl
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, Sienna Park <sienna@medicosys.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 May 2025 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: March session traces + KV-cache linkage and signed manifest

Hi all —

A few operational details to lock down the sampling/retention and manifest signing approach:

Sampling and retention
- Default retention for request-level telemetry is 90 days in hot storage and 365 days in cold archive. For a one-off SOC2 export we can pull from cold archive; expected extra time for reconstruction ~24-48 hours beyond extraction time.
- If MedicoSys requests full request/response bodies for the whole month we will need a scoped exception to our normal throughput limits; estimate size 500GB-2TB depending on average prompt length.
- Recommended sampling: stratified 5% by user (random seed tied to user_hash) plus 20% of sessions flagged as high-cost (based on token count). This preserves signal for both breadth and heavy users.

Manifest & immutability
- Manifest content: export_id, file_list, checksum(SHA256), file_size_bytes, s3_path, created_at(iso8601), manifest_version, signer_cert_id.
- Signing: Redwood will sign the manifest using our signing cert (RFC 5280) and produce a signed PDF summary. For independent verification auditors can validate the SHA256s against the files.
- HMAC layer: if you prefer a shared-secret approach we can compute an HMAC-SHA256 over the manifest and deliver the HMAC key via your public PGP key.

Packaging & delivery
- Evidence will be staged in a dedicated bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/medicosys/2025-03-kv-export/. Objects will be write-once; we will enable object lock for governance controls during transfer.
- We will provide a manifest_v1.json (signed) plus signed_manifest_v1.pdf as a human-readable signature bundle.
- Checksums will be provided as both SHA256 and CRC32c for compatibility with older tooling.

Next steps
- Marcus, I recommend we prepare a small scoped sample (7 days) and the manifest within 48 hours for MedicoSys to review. If they confirm full-month exports we issue a formal evidence Handoff document and apply object lock on the bucket.

Questions for MedicoSys: please provide PGP public key for compliance@medicosys.com and confirm whether you need reversible salts held by Redwood (we strongly recommend you keep the salt).

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Principal Product Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
